address: Kim San Leng Coffee Shop, Blk 511 Bishan Street 13, S570511
w: The stall most synonymous with Bishan — a 40-plus-year institution beside Bishan Bus Interchange whose chicken is plunged into ice water after poaching for a signature gelatinous skin and tender flesh, drawing snaking queues onto its iconic green plates.

dish: Handmade coin roti prata with fish/mutton curry
address: Jin Fa Kopitiam, 24 Sin Ming Road, #01-51, S570024
w: A third-generation Sin Ming stall where two brothers flip dough hand-made fresh every evening — famous for round, thick, crispy 'coin prata' rarely sold elsewhere and curries done as well as the prata; featured by the Michelin Guide's roti prata round-up.

dish: Teochew peppery bak kut teh with 'dragon ribs'
n: Rong Cheng (Sin Ming Road) Bak Kut Teh
w: Uncle Lim has served peppery Teochew bak kut teh here since 1976 and pioneered the use of 'dragon ribs' — the 16 largest rib bones in a pig — in a clear, garlicky, pepper-forward broth that made this remote Sin Ming shop a pilgrimage.

dish: Hakka suan pan zi (yam abacus seeds)
address: Shunfu Mart Food Centre, #02-26, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320
w: Run by the Toh sisters since the 1980s, this Shunfu stall makes suan pan zi (abacus seeds) with a texture like no other — chewy yam-and-flour discs stir-fried with dried shrimp, minced pork, mushroom and crispy shallots, a hard-to-find Hakka classic.

dish: Bak chor mee with house-fried fishballs & braised pork trotter
address: Gourmet Street Coffeeshop, Blk 22 Sin Ming Road, S570022
w: A decades-old Sin Ming heartland stall whose twist is its fishballs — bought fresh daily then fried in the stall's own special oil for a light, springy, browned bite — served over minced-pork noodles with optional braised trotter and intestines.

dish: Shanxi dao xiao mian (hand-shaved knife-cut noodles)
address: Bishan Cafeteria, Bishan Bus Interchange (beside Junction 8), Bishan Place, Singapore
w: Owner Liu Yi Jun was Crystal Jade's La Mian Director for nearly 30 years before opening this humble Shanxi stall atop Bishan Bus Interchange — freshly hand-shaved dao xiao mian and springy la mian in a clear beef-bone broth, plus mala braised-meat noodles.

The Bishan zi char hotspot that takes over the whole coffeeshop at dinner — its lobster chee cheong fun (silky rice rolls under tender lobster and savoury sauce) won the SPH Food Masters award in 2020; the salt-baked crab is the other must-order.

address: Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320
w: A Shunfu Mart mainstay plating a classic $3.90 Hainanese chicken rice with succulent poached chicken and fragrant, faintly crusty rice — a fixture on every guide to the recently renovated hawker centre.

address: Shunfu Mart Food Centre, #02-20, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320
w: A long-queuing Shunfu char kway teow stall dishing generous $3 plates of sweet-savoury noodles studded with fresh cockles — one of the food centre's most popular names across post-renovation guides.

dish: Teochew kway chap with braised offal
w: One of Bishan's oldest hawker stalls and a cult supper spot — opening in the evening and running into the small hours, its flat rice sheets come with a glossy braise of clean-tasting pig offal that keeps a queue going past midnight.

dish: Mushroom minced-meat noodles & fish maw soup
n: Ding Ji Mushroom Minced Meat Noodle
w: A Bishan Street 22 coffeeshop stall touted as a worthy alternative to Seng Kee — bak chor mee and a hearty $8 fish maw soup with generous minced pork, pork balls and a higher-grade fish maw in a pork-bone broth.

address: Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320
w: An ex-hotel pastry chef bakes large, moist, fragrant muffins from around $1.50-$2.20 at this Shunfu stall — the Blueberry and Coffee Walnut draw consistent lines, a rare hawker-priced bakery gem.

dish: Nasi lemak, mee rebus & mee siam
address: Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320
w: Shunfu Mart's comforting no-frills Malay stall running the gamut from nasi lemak to mee rebus, mee soto and lontong — the mee siam, sweet-sour and generously topped, is the pick.

address: Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320
w: Serving traditional prawn noodles for over 45 years, Quan Ann favours a lighter pork-based broth — the dry version with its robust sauce mix and house-made chilli paste is the crowd favourite at Shunfu.

address: Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320
w: A lunchtime-queue stall at Shunfu ladling out refreshing bowls of sliced fish and fried fish soup loaded with vegetables and topped with fried egg — a light, comforting Teochew standard.

address: Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320
w: An unlikely two-in-one Shunfu stall pairing $1.70 handmade popiah with a bowl of fishball noodles — regulars order both — that Daniel Food Diary and Makansutra both flag among the food centre's keepers.

address: Food Junction, Junction 8, 9 Bishan Place, #04-01, S579837
w: The Singapore arm of Hong Kong's one-Michelin-star Kam's Roast Goose brings quality Cantonese roast meats to Bishan — roast duck, char siew and crispy roast pork rice from $7.80, with a hefty roast duck drumstick rice at $10.80.

A wallet-friendly Bishan-area Thai institution since 1999, serving affordable, honest, family-recipe Thai — zi-char-style plates like phad thai seafood and tom yum seafood well under $10; a long-running student and family staple.
